top3.headline: Anthropic files to go public
top3.whyItMatters: Your key AI vendor will soon publish its costs and risks; read the prospectus closely.

top3.headline: United shuts the door on unauthorized AI agents
top3.whyItMatters: Big brands can block your agents; plan agent access as a partnership, not a given.

top3.headline: One Home Repo lets agents work across every repo
top3.whyItMatters: Multi-repo work is where agents stall; this pattern gives them a single map.

items.title: Anthropic files its IPO registration with the SEC
items.takeaway: Anthropic says it has filed a registration statement, including a prospectus, for its initial public offering.
items.soWhat: A public Anthropic will disclose costs and risks; read the prospectus before your next model contract.

items.title: Matt Pocock: one Home Repo to run agents across all repos
items.takeaway: He publishes the Home Repo pattern for multi-repo agent work, with a setup prompt to run on your org's repos.
items.soWhat: Agents stall at repo boundaries; a single home repo gives them one map of your whole codebase.

items.title: Naval: someone, somewhere, will build the datacenters
items.takeaway: He calls datacenters a globally competitive market and says someone, somewhere, will build them.
items.soWhat: Compute supply is global; local limits shift where capacity lands, not whether it exists.

items.title: T3 Code passes 1,000 open source contributors
items.takeaway: Theo says it is one of the biggest open source iPhone apps and non-developers ask him how to set it up.
items.soWhat: Coding agents are reaching non-developers; expect staff outside engineering to ask for them.

items.title: Meng To shares a full tutorial for his three.js apartment
items.takeaway: He walks through recreating his apartment in three.js with Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2.
items.soWhat: Designers can now ship interactive 3D with agents; a tutorial makes it repeatable for teams.

items.title: Open-weight models are under 0.5% of T3 Code traffic
items.takeaway: Theo says open-weight models are a tiny share of usage on his coding app, and the claim drew little pushback.
items.soWhat: Developers are paying for closed frontier models; weigh that before betting on open-weight savings.

items.title: ThePrimeagen: after weeks of vibe coding, each change takes hours
items.takeaway: He says heavy vibe coding left him with a codebase where every change now takes three hours.
items.soWhat: Speed without structure turns into drag; ask teams how they keep agent-written code maintainable.

items.title: Nvidia's board reportedly prepares to fire CEO Jensen Huang
items.takeaway: The WSJ reports the board may meet today after a second alleged affair; shares fell over 7% after hours.
items.soWhat: Key-person risk at the top AI chip supplier is now live; review your compute exposure.

items.title: United won't let unauthorized AI agents book flights
items.takeaway: The Verge reports United is refusing bookings made by unauthorized AI agents.
items.soWhat: Agent access is now a business decision; check which partners will block your customer-facing agents.

items.title: AI agent web traffic grew 8x from August to October
items.takeaway: a16z cites HUMAN Security; The Verge reports United won't let AI agents book flights.
items.soWhat: Decide now whether agents are customers you serve or traffic you block.

related.name: a16z: Welcome to the B2A Economy

items.title: Theo: Gemini 4 Carbon took 22 minutes, Opus 5.5 under 10
items.takeaway: He says most of the delay is server side, with 11 seconds before the first response.
items.soWhat: Benchmark scores hide latency; time models on your own tasks before switching.

items.title: a16z: H100 rental rates run 54% above expected depreciation
items.takeaway: As of Oct 19, A100s sat 9% and H100s 54% above a six-year straight-line path.
items.soWhat: Compute keeps its value longer than planned, so budget for rental prices staying high.

items.title: Perplexity: general models beat cyber models at breaking its agent sandbox
items.takeaway: Red-teaming SPACE, GPT 5.6 Sol found exploits better than GPT 5.6 Sol Cyber.
items.soWhat: Test agent sandboxes with your strongest general model, not only specialist security tools.

items.title: Google launches an API that scores 1,000 choices in one pass
items.takeaway: Gemini Decision 1 picks from closed sets across text, images, audio, video and PDFs.
items.soWhat: Triage, tagging and routing are closed-set choices; test whether this beats your current setup.

items.title: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how mutations act in specific cells
items.takeaway: Trained on 100M+ cell profiles; free for academic research via API, private preview for commercial use.
items.soWhat: AI for science is becoming a research tool; health and pharma teams should test access now.

items.title: Google tests Tabletop for building custom collaboration apps
items.takeaway: The Verge covers Google's Tabletop AI experiment, its waitlist and availability.
items.soWhat: Teams may soon build their own shared tools; watch for shadow apps outside IT.

items.title: A family runs its shared AI brain on Claude Code and Obsidian
items.takeaway: Lenny's Newsletter features Scott Farrar on using Claude Code with Obsidian as a family knowledge base.
items.soWhat: Coding agents now manage plain notes, not just code; the pattern fits team knowledge too.

items.title: Meng To turns his three.js game into a trailer with Fable 5.2
items.takeaway: He shared a 60-second trailer the model made from his game.
items.soWhat: Marketing assets can now come from the product itself, cutting design cycles.

items.title: VulnCheck: Glasswing logged 37,966 findings, only 217 marked fixed
items.takeaway: It counts 442 CVEs tied to Anthropic, two exploited; curl rejected 19 of 34 scanner reports.
items.soWhat: AI finds bugs faster than people can verify and fix them, so budget for triage.

items.title: Lyn Alden: wary of Huang's tenure, bullish on 2027 GPU demand
items.takeaway: She calls herself neutral to bearish on Huang as CEO and bullish on GPU demand in 2027.
items.soWhat: A respected macro voice separates Nvidia's leadership risk from the demand for AI compute.

items.title: Nathan Benaich: defenders need open cyber models too
items.takeaway: He says Hugging Face found API guardrails slowed an intrusion probe and used a self-hosted open model.
items.soWhat: Closed-model guardrails can block your own security team; keep an open-model option for incidents.

voices.quote: You'd think we'd have learned from Steve Jobs and Travis Kalanick that one does not just simply replace the founder…
So I have been vibing. Going hard. Now every change takes 3 hours.. wtf this sucks
Datacenters are a globally competitive market. Someone, somewhere, will build them.
I just told my agent "treat me like a tool call". So degrading

hotOnX.text: You'd think we'd have learned from Steve Jobs and Travis Kalanick that one does not just simply replace the founder…
hotOnX.note: The Huang reports reopened the old fight over whether boards should remove founders.

hotOnX.text: Who benefits from the timing of the Huang stories? Taking out the premier champion of open models helps those who want AI closed.
hotOnX.note: It frames the Nvidia fight as a battle over open versus closed AI.

hotOnX.text: So I have been vibing. Going hard. Now every change takes 3 hours.. wtf this sucks
hotOnX.note: Many builders recognize the hidden cost of fast, unstructured agent coding.

hotOnX.text: Open weight models make up less than 0.5% of T3 Code traffic, and saying so now gets crickets.
hotOnX.note: A rare usage number on how little developers use open models in practice.

hotOnX.text: Datacenters are a globally competitive market. Someone, somewhere, will build them.
hotOnX.note: Investors are debating whether any single country can control where AI compute gets built.
